issues.legal_issue: The arrangements for additional agents, purchasers, and the transport of growers’ leaves were not shown to invalidate or undermine the state monopoly in the trade.
material_facts: The challenged amendments and rules enabled additional agents and purchasers and permitted registered growers to transport leaves outside their unit for sale to an authorized buyer.
The agents purchased leaves from growers at prices fixed by the Government and delivered processed leaves as directed by forest officers.
Only the State Forest Corporation had been appointed as an additional agent, and no additional purchasers had been appointed.
issues.conclusion: The challenged arrangements were not per se invalid; they appeared necessary to enable the Government to control the monopoly business effectively, and the petitioners did not show that they operated against the Government’s monopoly.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 14 and 19(1)(g), a state monopoly must be operated for the public benefit and not as a means of conferring private benefits. Akadasi Pradhan v. State of Orissa upheld the monopoly and the use of agents acting on the Government’s behalf, while invalidating a rule that left their terms to arbitrary discretion. Rashbehari Panda v. State of Orissa held that restricting offers to a limited class of existing contractors was discriminatory. The challenged arrangements here were not shown to have that effect.

rule.if: monopoly_scheme_challenge and government_sets_grower_purchase_price and government_directs_disposal_of_processed_goods and (additional_agents_meet_operational_needs or growers_transport_leaves_only_for_authorized_sale)

predicates.monopoly_scheme_challenge: A person challenges arrangements governing a state monopoly on the ground that they undermine the monopoly or discriminate against traders.
predicates.government_sets_grower_purchase_price: The government fixes the price at which agents purchase the goods from growers.
predicates.government_directs_disposal_of_processed: Government officers direct to whom agents must deliver processed goods.
predicates.additional_agents_meet_operational_needs: Additional agents are appointed to meet operational needs in carrying on the government-controlled trade.
predicates.growers_transport_leaves_only_for_author: Growers may transport their goods outside their local area only to sell them to a buyer authorized under the government-controlled arrangement.

issues.definition: When a monopoly-scheme challenge concerns a trade in which the government fixes purchase prices and directs disposal, the arrangements are not invalid as undermining the monopoly if additional agents meet operational needs or growers’ transport is confined to authorized sales.

issues.legal_issue: An agent’s relationship with, or nomination by, a purchaser does not by itself defeat a state monopoly when the agent performs the Government’s controlled purchasing and delivery functions.
material_facts: The petitioners alleged that some agents were nominees or relations of purchasers.
Agents had to buy leaves from growers at Government-fixed prices and deliver processed leaves as forest officers directed.
The agents’ charges and remuneration were fixed under the arrangement.
issues.conclusion: The alleged relationship between agents and purchasers did not, by itself, affect the state monopoly or show that the agents were acting for purchasers rather than the Government.
issues.legal_principle: Akadasi Pradhan v. State of Orissa permits agents to carry on a state monopoly when they act on the Government’s behalf and for its benefit, rather than for their own benefit. The Court applied that principle to the agents’ actual duties and regulated remuneration; it did not treat a relationship with a purchaser alone as sufficient to invalidate the arrangement.

rule.if: state_monopoly_challenge and agent_buys_at_government_fixed_prices and agent_delivers_as_officials_direct and agent_compensation_is_fixed

predicates.state_monopoly_challenge: A person challenges whether an agent arrangement is compatible with a government-operated monopoly.
predicates.agent_buys_at_government_fixed_prices: The agent purchases goods from growers at prices fixed by the government.
predicates.agent_delivers_as_officials_direct: The agent delivers processed goods to recipients directed by government officials.
predicates.agent_compensation_is_fixed: The agent’s charges or remuneration are fixed under the arrangement.

issues.definition: If an agent in a state-monopoly challenge buys at government-fixed prices, delivers as officials direct, and receives fixed compensation, the agent’s relationship with a purchaser alone does not defeat the monopoly.

issues.legal_issue: The Government was not required to accept the highest tender and could prefer a lower tenderer on an overall assessment of suitability.
material_facts: In some units, persons whose tenders were lower were asked to raise their offers to the highest price before their tenders were accepted.
The Government preferred some tenderers on considerations including past experience and a clean record.
The Government rejected some high tenders because of default, failure to provide a required guarantee, or other unsuitability.
issues.conclusion: The Government was not bound to accept the highest tender and could accept a lower tender when, on an overall consideration, it preferred that tenderer; the preferences shown did not establish an unlawful choice.
issues.legal_principle: In considering a challenge under Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) to public contracting, the Government need not accept the highest tender and may prefer another tenderer on an overall assessment, including experience and past conduct. Rashbehari Panda v. State of Orissa condemned a scheme that restricted the opportunity to offer to a limited class; it did not require acceptance of the highest offer in every tender process.

predicates.public_tender_challenge: A person challenges the government’s selection of a tenderer for a public contract.
predicates.lower_tenderer_was_preferred_on_overall_: The government preferred a tenderer with a lower initial offer after considering suitability, such as experience or past conduct.
predicates.lower_tenderer_was_required_to_match_the: The government required the selected tenderer to raise the offer to the highest price before accepting it.

issues.definition: When a lower tenderer is preferred on overall merits and required to match the highest offer, the existence of a higher initial tender does not alone make the government’s choice unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: The evidence did not establish that the tender selections were arbitrary, discriminatory, or made to obtain political contributions for the party in power.
material_facts: The petitioners alleged that political contributions had been demanded as a condition of accepting tenders and that favored persons were selected.
The Minister and the legislator identified in the allegations denied that any such demand had been made.

The Government’s account showed that most units were settled at the highest prices offered, while other departures from that course were explained by matters such as experience, default, failed guarantees, withdrawn tenders, or lack of tenders.
The challenged petitions concerned seven units.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners did not prove the alleged political-contribution demands or arbitrary and mala fide preferences; the Government’s account of the settlements defeated the suggestion of fraudulent preference.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) protect against discriminatory or unreasonable restrictions, and Rashbehari Panda v. State of Orissa establishes that a plea of bona fides alone does not answer a demonstrated infringement of fundamental rights. Here, however, the allegations were denied and the tender record did not establish the asserted infringement; the Court found the alleged mala fides and arbitrary preference unproved.

rule.if: tender_selection_challenge and political_contribution_demand_is_alleged and officials_deny_the_demand and tender_records_explain_departures_from_highest_offers

predicates.tender_selection_challenge: A person challenges government selections made through a tender process as arbitrary or mala fide.
predicates.political_contribution_demand_is_alleged: A challenger alleges that officials required a political contribution in exchange for accepting a tender.
predicates.officials_deny_the_demand: The officials accused of making the demand deny that it occurred.
predicates.tender_records_explain_departures_from_h: The tender record gives case-specific reasons for selections that did not go to the highest initial offer.

issues.definition: In a tender-selection challenge, an alleged political contribution demand and departures from the highest offers do not establish mala fides or arbitrary preference when officials deny the demand and the tender records explain the departures.
